mainTopic: Wine and appetite, רב ששת's fast on ערב פסח, and the laws of הסיבה at the סדר
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier debate: does wine fill you up (מסעד סעיד) or make you hungrier (מגרר גריר)? The גמרא proves from a משנה about extra drinking between the cups that wine whets the appetite. Next it reports that רב ששת fasted all day on ערב פסח. The גמרא suggests a legal reason: the eating ban protects the קרבן פסח, and בן בתירא allows the פסח all day. It then rejects this, because רב ששת was simply delicate and needed an appetite at night. The amud then turns to הסיבה (reclining). מצה needs הסיבה, מרור does not, and all four cups need it. It explains that one must lean left, not on the back or to the right. It then rules on who must recline: a wife, a son, a תלמיד before his רב, and a שמש. Finally, רבי יהושע בן לוי says women are obligated in the four cups, and the reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about drinking between the four cups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: between the first cups you may drink extra wine, but between the third and fourth cups you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between these cups, if a person wants to drink, he may drink. Between the third and the fourth, he may not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from a later משנה in פסחים about the four cups. It is setting up a proof for the debate about whether wine fills you up or whets the appetite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud (107b) the question was open: does wine fill a person up, or does it make him hungrier? This משנה allows extra wine before the meal, between the early cups. It forbids extra wine after the meal, between the third and fourth cups. The גמרא will use the first part to build its proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Cups, meaning the four cups of the סדר
Between the third and the fourth cup

phrases.english: Between these cups
phrases.notes: The early cups, which come before the meal

phrases.english: if he wants to drink, he may drink,
between the third and the fourth, he may not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין הַכּוֹסוֹת הַלָּלוּ אִם רָצָה לִשְׁתּוֹת יִשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source into the earlier debate (on the previous amud) about whether wine fills or whets the appetite
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether wine fills a person up or whets the appetite
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting extra drinking between the early cups of the סדר

steps.title: If wine filled you up, extra cups would ruin the מצה
steps.stepSummary: If wine fills a person up, the משנה should not allow extra wine before the meal, because he would then eat the מצה when already full.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say wine fills a person up, why may he drink? He will end up eating the מצה as overeating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that wine fills you up, using the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצה must be eaten with appetite. Eating it when already stuffed is called אכילה גסה, and that is not a proper מצוה eating. If extra wine filled a person up, the משנה would never allow it before the מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It satisfies, meaning wine fills a person up

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה lets you drink because wine doesn't matter. The point is the reverse: the timing of the wine matters a lot, because the מצה must be eaten with appetite.

phrases.english: And if you say it (wine) satisfies,
why may he drink?
He will be eating the matzah
as excessive (overfull) eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מִסְעָד סָעֵיד אַמַּאי יִשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 1 to attack the view that wine fills a person up
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that wine fills a person up (מסעד סעיד)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wine filled you up, drinking extra before the meal would lead to eating the מצה as אכילה גסה. Yet the משנה allows it.

steps.title: Conclusion: wine whets the appetite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that wine makes a person hungrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: wine whets the appetite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the proof: wine does not fill you up, it makes you hungrier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה allows extra wine before the מצה, the wine must not hurt the appetite. In fact it helps it. That settles the debate in favor of מגרר גריר.

keyTerms.meaning: It whets, meaning wine stirs up the appetite

steps.whatToRemember: Wine before the meal stirs up the appetite (מגרר גריר). That is why extra drinking between the early cups is allowed: it does not ruin the eating of the מצה.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
it (wine) whets the appetite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the proof built in steps 1 and 2

steps.title: רב ששת fasted the entire day before פסח
steps.stepSummary: A report that רב ששת fasted the whole day of ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would sit in a fast the whole day of ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It reports that רב ששת fasted all day on ערב פסח, and it will next ask why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (פסחים צט:) only forbids eating from close to מנחה time. רב ששת went much further and did not eat even in the morning. The question is what reasoning could lead him to such a strict practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve of a day, the day before
He would sit, meaning he would regularly do this

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would sit in a fast
the entire eve of Passover.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא כׇּל מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִסְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a practice related to the ban on eating on ערב פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת fasted all day on ערב פסח

steps.title: Suggested reason, part one: the ban is about the Pesach offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב ששת held two things. First, the משנה's ban starts at מנחה גדולה. Second, the reason is so a person does not get carried away with his meal and miss the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רב ששת holds: we learned the ban as close to מנחה גדולה, and the reason is the פסח, lest he be drawn into his meal and come to hold back from doing the פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to propose an explanation for רב ששת's fast. This is the first half of a two-part suggestion, and the second half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says not to eat 'close to מנחה,' and there are two ways to read it. One reading is מנחה גדולה, which is early afternoon, as opposed to מנחה קטנה, which is late afternoon. The suggestion picks the early time and ties the ban to protecting the קרבן פסח, not just to eating the מצה with appetite. That links the ban to whenever the פסח may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a proposed explanation)
The early afternoon time, half an hour after midday
Lest he be drawn along (into his meal)
To refrain or hold back from

steps.confusionAlert: נימא is only a suggestion, not the final word. Step 8 rejects it: רב ששת fasted for a personal health reason.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Sheshet holds:
we learned 'close to the greater minchah'
and it is because of the Paschal lamb,
lest he be drawn along (in his meal)
and come to refrain from performing the Paschal lamb,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes reasoning behind the fast reported in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What view would lead רב ששת to fast the entire day of ערב פסח?
steps.whyThisMatters: If the ban on eating exists to protect the קרבן פסח, then the time of the ban depends on when the פסח may be brought. That sets up the next step.

steps.title: Suggested reason, part two: בן בתירא allows the פסח from morning
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the suggestion: רב ששת agreed with בן בתירא that a פסח slaughtered in the morning of the fourteenth is valid. So the whole day is פסח time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he holds like what רבי אושעיא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: בן בתירא would declare valid a פסח slaughtered in the morning of the fourteenth for its own sake. From the morning it is already פסח time, since the whole day is fit for the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the second piece of its suggestion. Combined with step 5, this would explain an all-day fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the פסח is brought in the afternoon. בן בתירא says that even a morning slaughter, done for the sake of a פסח, is valid. If the ban on eating protects the פסח, and the פסח can be brought from morning, then eating is banned from morning too.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake (slaughtered as a פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: בן בתירא does not say the פסח should ideally be brought in the morning. He only says that if it was, it is valid, because the morning already counts as פסח time.

phrases.english: And he holds like this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Oshaya said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Ben Beteira would declare valid
a Paschal lamb that was slaughtered in the morning
on the fourteenth, for its own sake,
and from the morning it is the time of the Paschal lamb,
since the whole day is fit for the Paschal lamb,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part suggestion begun in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב ששת's fast reflects combining the 'because of the פסח' reason with בן בתירא's all-day time for the פסח
steps.whyThisMatters: Put together, steps 5 and 6 explain the all-day fast. The פסח time starts in the morning, so the eating ban starts in the morning too.

steps.title: Ben Beteira's reading of 'bein ha'arbayim'
steps.stepSummary: בן בתירא reads the Torah's phrase בין הערבים as 'between last evening and this evening,' which covers the whole day of the fourteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: For he holds that בין הערבים means between the evening of yesterday and the evening of today.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where בן בתירא gets his view. He reads the Torah's words בין הערבים as covering the entire day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most read בין הערבים as 'the afternoon,' the time between the sun starting to drop and nightfall. בן בתירא reads it as the full stretch between two evenings, from last night to tonight. That makes the whole fourteenth valid for the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Between the evenings' (שמות יב:ו), the Torah's time for the פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion for רב ששת's fast has two parts. First, the eating ban protects the קרבן פסח. Second, following בן בתירא, the פסח may be brought all day, because בין הערבים means 'between last evening and this evening.' So eating would be banned all day.

phrases.english: For he holds that 'between the evenings' means
between the evening of yesterday
and the evening of today.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּסָבַר בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם בֵּין עֶרֶב דְּאֶתְמוֹל לְעֶרֶב דְּהָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for בן בתירא's view cited in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בן בתירא reads בין הערבים as the full day of the fourteenth. This completes the proposed reasoning for רב ששת's fast, which the next passage will evaluate.

steps.title: רב ששת fasted for a personal reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from steps 5-7. רב ששת fasted because he was delicate: if he ate anything in the morning, he could not enjoy his food at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: No. רב ששת is different, because he was delicate. If he tasted anything in the morning, his food at night would not do him any good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רב ששת's all-day fast proves anything about the law. It gives a personal, health-based reason for his fast instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-7 tried to build a legal position from רב ששת's practice: the ban begins at מנחה גדולה, and he agreed with בן בתירא. This rejection removes that proof. His fast was a private health matter, so that he could eat the מצה at night with an appetite. It does not show which opinion he held.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's fast was a personal health measure. It is not proof that the ban starts at מנחה גדולה or that he followed בן בתירא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from this story that everyone must fast all day on ערב פסח. The גמרא says explicitly that רב ששת's case was unusual.

phrases.english: They say: No,
Rav Sheshet is different, for he was delicate,
for if he tasted anything in the morning,

phrases.aramaic: לְאוּרְתָּא לָא הֲוָה מַהְנֵי לֵיהּ מֵיכְלָא.
phrases.english: at night the food would not be beneficial to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference about רב ששת's legal position that was built in steps 5-7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that רב ששת's fast reveals his legal views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fast can be explained by his delicate health, so it proves nothing about his legal opinion.

steps.title: הסיבה: מצה yes, מרור no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that even a poor person must recline. It then reports that מצה requires הסיבה and מרור does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: even the poorest Jew should not eat until he reclines. It was stated: מצה requires reclining; מרור does not require reclining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה, about reclining. It states the basic rules for מצה and מרור, which sets up the question about wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reclining is a sign of a free person, so the food that represents freedom, מצה, requires it. מרור stands for the bitterness of slavery, so it does not need reclining. These two clear rules set the stage for wine, which is less clear.

phrases.english: And even the poorest of Israel
shall not eat until he reclines.
It was stated: matza requires reclining,
bitter herbs do not require reclining.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיָּסֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה requires הסיבה; מרור does not.

steps.title: Two opposite reports about wine
steps.stepSummary: Two reports in the name of רב נחמן contradict each other. One says wine requires הסיבה, and the other says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding wine: it was stated in the name of רב נחמן that it requires reclining. And it was stated in the name of רב נחמן that it does not require reclining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents two reports from the same Sage that say opposite things. This sets up a problem that the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine falls between מצה and מרור, and it is not obvious whether it requires reclining. The real difficulty is that רב נחמן seems to say both yes and no. The next step must explain how one person could hold both positions.

phrases.english: Wine — it was stated in the name of Rav Nachman:
it requires reclining.
And it was stated in the name of Rav Nachman:
it does not require reclining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reclining discussion to wine and exposes a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two reports in the name of רב נחמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same Sage cannot say both that wine requires reclining and that it does not.

steps.title: Each report refers to different cups
steps.stepSummary: The reports do not really argue. One is about the first two cups and the other is about the last two cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This one is about the first two cups, and that one is about the last two cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each statement to a different pair of the four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports are true, because each covers only two of the four cups. This answer leaves an open question: which pair requires reclining? The next steps deal with that question.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this is regarding the first two cups,
that is regarding the last two cups.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא בְּתַרְתֵּי כָּסֵי קַמָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases (each statement covers a different pair of cups)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן contradicted himself about wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: One pair of cups requires הסיבה and the other pair does not.

steps.title: Version one: the first two cups need reclining
steps.stepSummary: There are two versions of which pair needs הסיבה. In the first version, the first two cups need it because freedom is beginning. The last two do not, because the freedom already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it one way and some say it the other way. Some say it this way: the first two cups require reclining, because that is when freedom begins. The last two cups do not require reclining, because what happened has happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that people disagreed about which pair of cups needs reclining. It then gives the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, reclining marks the moment freedom starts. That happens during the first part of the סדר, while we tell the story of leaving Egypt. By the last two cups the story is finished, so there is no special need to show freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was (it is already done)

phrases.english: Some say it this way
and some say it that way.
Some say it this way:
the first two cups require reclining,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַשְׁתָּא הוּא דְּקָא מַתְחֲלָא לַהּ חֵירוּת.
phrases.english: for it is now that freedom begins.

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי כָּסֵי בָּתְרָאֵי — לָא בָּעוּ הֲסִיבָּה,
phrases.english: The last two cups do not require reclining,
what was, was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which pair of cups from step 11 requires reclining, according to the first version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Specifying which case each statement applies to
steps.terutzMaskana: First version: the first two cups require הסיבה, and the last two do not.

steps.title: Version two: the last two cups need reclining
steps.stepSummary: The second version says the opposite. The last two cups need הסיבה because by then we are free. The first two do not, because we are still saying עבדים היינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say it the other way: On the contrary, the last two cups require reclining, because that is the time of freedom. The first two cups do not require reclining, because a person is still saying 'We were slaves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version, which reverses the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here reclining belongs to the time when freedom is complete, which is the second half of the סדר. At the first two cups we are still telling about slavery (עבדים היינו), so reclining does not fit yet. Both versions agree that reclining means freedom; they only disagree about when freedom is felt during the סדר.

phrases.english: And some say it that way:

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, תְּרֵי כָּסֵי בָּתְרָאֵי — בָּעוּ הֲסִיבָּה,
phrases.english: On the contrary, the last two cups require reclining,
that is the time when there is freedom.

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי כָּסֵי קַמָּאֵי — לָא בָּעוּ הֲסִיבָּה,
phrases.english: The first two cups do not require reclining,
for he is still saying 'We were slaves.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite assignment of the cups from the one in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: Second version: the last two cups require הסיבה, and the first two do not.

steps.title: All four cups require reclining
steps.stepSummary: Since both versions were reported and we cannot decide between them, the הלכה is that all four cups require הסיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that it was stated this way and it was stated that way, both these and those require reclining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling. Because we do not know which version is right, we recline for all four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of cups requires reclining according to one of the two versions. To satisfy both versions, we recline for every cup. This is a practical solution to a doubt, not a sign that both versions were originally the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that it was said this way and that way

steps.whatToRemember: מצה requires הסיבה and מרור does not. All four cups of wine require הסיבה, because we follow both versions of רב נחמן's opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of reclining while drinking every one of the four cups at the סדר.

phrases.english: Now that it was stated this way and stated that way,
both these and those require reclining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt between the two versions in steps 12 and 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All four cups of wine require הסיבה.

steps.title: Lying on the back or leaning right is not proper reclining
steps.stepSummary: Two positions do not count as הסיבה: lying flat on the back and leaning to the right. Leaning right is also dangerous because food may go down the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lying on your back is not called reclining. Leaning to the right is not called reclining. Also, leaning right might make the windpipe open before the food pipe, and the person could choke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what counts as proper הסיבה. It names two positions that do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know all four cups need הסיבה, so we need to know how to do it correctly. A פרקדן lies flat, which is not how free people eat. Leaning right fails for two reasons: it is not the normal free-person style, and it creates a choking danger (סכנה).

keyTerms.meaning: Reclining, leaning to the side like a free person
Someone lying flat on his back

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of leaning to the left at the סדר.
steps.confusionAlert: The text only says that leaning RIGHT does not count. Leaning left is the correct way because of this rule. It is not a separate statement in the text.

phrases.english: Lying on one's back is not called reclining.
Reclining to the right is not called reclining.
And not only that, but
perhaps the windpipe will come before the esophagus,
and he will come into danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled that all four cups need הסיבה, the גמרא now defines what proper הסיבה is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lying on the back and leaning right are not valid הסיבה. Leaning right is also a choking hazard.

steps.title: Who must recline: a wife and a son
steps.stepSummary: A wife eating with her husband does not need to recline, unless she is an אשה חשובה. A son eating with his father must recline.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman with her husband does not need to recline. But if she is an important woman, she must recline. A son with his father must recline.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from how to recline to who must recline. It gives rulings for a wife and for a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife is normally treated as under her husband's household authority, so full free-person reclining is not expected of her. An אשה חשובה is independent in her own right, so she reclines. A son must recline even though he respects his father, so respect alone does not cancel the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Next to, in the presence of

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה אֵצֶל בַּעְלָהּ לָא בָּעֲיָא הֲסִיבָּה,
phrases.english: A woman with her husband does not require reclining,
but if she is an important woman,
she requires reclining.
A son with his father requires reclining.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה אֵצֶל בַּעְלָהּ לָא בָּעֲיָא הֲסִיבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the laws of הסיבה, now about which people are obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife is exempt unless she is an אשה חשובה. A son with his father is obligated.

steps.title: What about a student with his teacher?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a תלמיד eating with his רב must recline.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law for a student who is with his teacher?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about a student and his teacher. This sets up the next steps, which try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is unclear. A son must recline before his father, which suggests a student must too. But the fear a student owes his רב may be greater, and that fear may conflict with the relaxed posture of a free person.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
A student in the presence of his teacher

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A student with his teacher, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wife and son cases, the גמרא asks about an unclear case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a תלמיד in the presence of his רב is obligated in הסיבה.

steps.title: אביי reports that רב יוסף exempted students
steps.stepSummary: אביי recalls that his group reclined even on each other's knees at רבה's house. At רב יוסף's house they were told they need not recline, because fear of one's teacher is like fear of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear. אביי said: When we were at my master's house, we reclined on each other's knees. When we came to רב יוסף's house, he told us: You do not need to, because the fear of your teacher is like the fear of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story from אביי. רב יוסף ruled that a student does not recline before his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At רבה's house there was not enough room, but the students still reclined, even on one another's knees. רב יוסף told them this was unnecessary: a student must show his teacher deep awe, almost like awe of Heaven. That awe does not fit with leaning back like a free, independent person, so the student is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The fear of your teacher is like the fear of Heaven

phrases.english: Come and hear: Abaye said:
When we were at the house of the Master,
phrases.notes: 'מר' here refers to רבה, אביי's teacher.

phrases.english: we reclined on each other's knees,
when we came to the house of Rav Yosef,
he said to us: You do not need to,
the fear of your teacher is like the fear of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with a report.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רב יוסף, a תלמיד with his רב does not need הסיבה because of the awe he owes his teacher.

steps.title: A ברייתא says even a student must recline
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person reclines in front of anyone, even a student before his teacher. This contradicts רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A person reclines with everyone, and even a student with his teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names the exact case of a student with his teacher and says he must recline. A ברייתא carries more weight than an אמורא, so רב יוסף's exemption looks wrong.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A person reclines with everyone,
and even a student with his teacher!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that a תלמיד does not recline before his רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly obligates a student before his teacher, which directly contradicts רב יוסף.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a craftsman's apprentice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about an apprentice learning a trade, not a Torah student. So רב יוסף's ruling still stands for a תלמיד of Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a carpenter's apprentice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a different kind of 'student'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'student' in the ברייתא means someone learning a trade from a craftsman. He does not owe his instructor awe like the fear of Heaven, so he must recline. A Torah student before his רב is still exempt, as רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: When that ברייתא was taught (it was about...)

steps.whatToRemember: A Torah תלמיד before his רב is exempt from הסיבה because his awe is like the fear of Heaven. A trade apprentice must recline, a son before his father must recline, and a wife is exempt unless she is an אשה חשובה.

phrases.english: When that one was taught,
it was about a carpenter's apprentice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 19 and protects רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא refers to a different kind of student.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about a Torah student and his רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a trade apprentice. A Torah student before his רב is exempt from הסיבה.

steps.title: What is the rule for a waiter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a שמש, someone serving the meal, must recline.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What about a waiter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question in the same list. Does a שמש have to recline when he eats the מצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a תלמיד eating with his רב does not need to recline. A שמש is also in a lower, serving position, and he is busy working. So maybe he is exempt too, or maybe he still must recline like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
A waiter or attendant who serves the meal

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What about a waiter?
phrases.notes: Does a waiter need to recline?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another person to the list of who must recline, after the wife, the son, and the תלמיד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a שמש, who is in a serving role, is obligated in הסיבה.

steps.title: A waiter who ate מצה while reclining has fulfilled his obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן לוי: a שמש who ate a כזית of מצה while reclining has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A waiter who ate an olive-size piece of מצה while reclining has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question about the שמש. It quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says a שמש who ate מצה while reclining has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its face, the statement only tells us the positive case: reclining works. The גמרא will look closely at the words 'while reclining' in the next step to answer the question.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size amount, the minimum for the מצוה

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A waiter who ate an olive-size piece of matza
while he is reclining has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question about the שמש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי that a שמש who ate מצה while reclining fulfilled his obligation, which will be used to prove the answer.

steps.title: Reading the exact wording: only reclining works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the statement precisely: reclining, yes; not reclining, no. So a שמש needs הסיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was reclining, yes, he fulfilled it. If he was not reclining, no. Learn from this that he needs to recline.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the words 'while reclining.' Since רבי יהושע בן לוי mentioned reclining, it must mean that without reclining the שמש has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would רבי יהושע בן לוי add 'while reclining' if it did not matter? This tells us reclining is required. So a שמש is not exempt like the תלמיד; he must recline.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from the source)

phrases.english: Reclining, yes (he fulfilled it);
not reclining, no (he did not).
Learn from this: he requires reclining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the exact wording of the source just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That a שמש is obligated in הסיבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'כשהוא מיסב' in רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement, which imply that without reclining he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: Confirmed: a waiter must recline
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: a שמש needs הסיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof it just made. The question is closed: a שמש must recline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This second 'שמע מינה' is not a repeat of the proof. It is the גמרא's stamp of approval that the proof works and nobody can reject it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the two 'שמע מינה' lines as the same thing. The first one draws the conclusion; the second one confirms it is correct.
steps.whatToRemember: A שמש must recline when eating the מצה, unlike a תלמיד before his רב, who does not need to.

phrases.english: Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof drawn in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שמש is obligated in הסיבה.

steps.title: Women are obligated in the four cups
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says women are obligated in the ארבע כוסות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Women are obligated in these four cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement from the same רבי יהושע בן לוי, starting a new topic. Women must drink the ארבע כוסות at the סדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This switches from who must recline to who must drink the four cups. The statement is new because one might think women are exempt from this מצוה, since it has a set time. The reason for the rule continues right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The four cups of wine at the סדר

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that women drink the ארבע כוסות at the סדר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Women are obligated
in these four cups,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second statement from the same אמורא, starting a new topic about the ארבע כוסות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in the ארבע כוסות.
